## 固定收益開場主論述

8月24日美國公債上漲。油價走低，緩解眼前的通膨壓力；另有報導指出，政府可能動用現金餘額支應債券回購，也讓市場以較有利的角度解讀擴大後的長債回購計畫。漲勢集中於中長天期：2年期殖利率微降0.3個基點至4.234%，5年期下跌2.3個基點至4.402%，10年期下降3.7個基點至4.698%，30年期則下跌4.5個基點至5.227%。

殖利率曲線隨之趨平，扭轉部分上週五因經濟活動數據而起的賣壓。2年與10年期利差收窄3.4個基點至46.4個基點，2年與30年期利差縮小4.2個基點至99.3個基點。10年期實質殖利率下跌3.4個基點至2.368%，幾乎解釋全部名目殖利率變動；10年期損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.3個基點至2.33%。這顯示投資人調降了持有美債所要求的實質殖利率，但並未認定中期通膨前景已明顯改善。

油價帶來較直接的通膨降溫動能。即使美國財政部長Scott Bessent揚言懲罰持續與伊朗往來的國家，WTI仍下跌2.16%至$85.18，布蘭特原油下跌2.39%至$92.13。他所稱的「經濟版D-Day」幾乎沒有提供執行細節，原油因此守住跌幅。近期能源壓力一度推高通膨補償與全球殖利率，這次價格下跌則讓債市獲得喘息。

另一項支撐來自報導稱，財政部官員正考慮動用該部門$9,350億現金餘額的一部分，買回票息較高的舊券。若以現金支應，就不必為每筆回購立即增發國庫券；相較於單純以短債替換長債，近期供給結構會更有利於長天期債券。報導出爐後，美債擴大漲幅，紐約午後10年期殖利率一度降至約4.69%。

不過，Bessent並未採納這項構想。他表示，擴大後的計畫尚未買進任何債券，例行標售將會持續，且11月初公布季度再融資安排前不會有所改變。因此，當日行情反映的是市場重新評價一種可能的籌資方式，並不代表財政部已承諾投入額外現金，或降低未來的借款需求。

利率市場以外也看得出這項區別。黃金期貨上漲2.47%至$4,738.20，一週漲幅達7.25%；美元指數當日上升0.18%，但全週仍下跌0.66%。長天期美債受惠於配套增發國庫券可能減少，但投資人同時評估，若政府一再干預債券殖利率，壓力是否終將轉移至匯率，因而持續尋求美元資產以外的替代選擇。

信用市場比股市穩定。投資級與高收益債券基金小幅上漲，標普500指數下跌0.28%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.97%。輝達即將公布財報之際，投資人重新評估AI投資熱潮所伴隨的融資負擔，費城半導體指數下跌2.70%，全週跌幅擴大至9.49%。美債上漲雖降低借款人的基準利率，但企業債供給與或有負債仍與政府爭奪資金。

## 現金支應回購仍是構想，尚非政策

財政部一般帳戶（TGA）的報導之所以重要，是因為它改變了前一週宣布之回購計畫可能採行的先後順序。交易商原先普遍預期，買回10至30年期舊券將透過增發國庫券籌資。這種做法雖會移除民間投資組合中的利率風險部位，市場上的債務總額卻大致不變，只是以一年內到期的證券取代較長天期債務。

動用現金可延後這項抵銷性發債。截至8月20日，TGA持有$9,350億；Morgan Stanley估計，視財政部如何界定超額現金而定，可動用金額可能介於$800億至$2,000億。即使取區間低端，也遠高於排定的長債回購規模。財政部表示，為支援流動性而進行的回購至少會加倍；依其日程，9月9日至11月4日期間，10至30年期債券的操作上限為$140億。

然而，帳面上的現金餘額不等於可任意用於支撐市場的資金。財政部將現金存放於聯準會，以支付從福利支出到員工及承包商款項等各類開支。自2015年起，其政策一直是保留至少足以支應五天開支或$1,500億的現金，以防債券市場中斷、無法取得融資。網路風險升高，加上每日支出存在不確定性，都強化了維持充足緩衝的理由。

動用TGA也只是把籌資需求移至未來，而非將其消除。用於回購的現金，最終仍須透過稅收、削減支出或日後舉債補回。眼前的好處是，財政部移除長天期債券時不必同步大量發債；後續影響則取決於現金餘額何時、以何種方式回補。因此，市場可以因這項報導而上漲，卻不會把$9,350億視為供給永久減少。

Bessent在記者會上保留了這份不確定性。他表示，財政部將維持例行標售，並未暗示會縮減附息債券的發行規模。他也說，9月9日啟動的新措施尚未進行任何買回。下一次季度再融資安排將於11月初公布，照例仍是財政部正式宣布重大標售、回購或現金管理政策變更的時點。

即使Bessent未作出新承諾，當日行情也沒有逆轉，因為籌資機制在邊際上仍有影響。現金相關報導出爐後，10年期殖利率降至約4.69%，跌幅約4個基點，接近當日收盤水準。30年期表現優於2年期，2年與30年期殖利率曲線趨平，顯示投資人仍賦予長端供給結構轉為有利一定機率。

交易規模顯示，這次調整並非發生在清淡市場。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.073兆，較上週五增加9.5%；名目附息債交易量增加4.7%至$8,713億。20年以上券種的成交量上升21.6%至$1,076億，10年以上至20年期區段則成長28.4%至$828億。這些資料無法判斷客戶是淨買方或淨賣方，但長端上漲確實伴隨交易量增加。

市場對介入的理由仍有爭議。Goldman Sachs策略師指出，擴大回購並未處理推升長天期殖利率的財政與通膨因素，即使加大規模，也不太可能實質重設利率水準。Wells Fargo認為，成長與通膨放緩、聯準會政策更明朗、財政整頓或投資級債券發行減少，才是可能帶來更持久殖利率下跌的催化因素。

市場運作情況也使財政部所稱的流動性理由更為複雜。JPMorgan研究發現，2026年前三個月，長天期美債的市場深度改善約38%，既受既有回購支撐，也得益於買方結構改變，包括更多高頻交易商參與。財政部擴大計畫時，交換利差與利率波動並未顯示市場運作異常失靈。這項政策仍可改善個別舊券的流動性，但宣布時點使投資人傾向將其視為對殖利率絕對水準的回應。

這種解讀可能推高期限溢價。季度日程公布僅兩週便突然改變安排，會削弱財政部債務管理一向具備的可預測性。若投資人預期未來的標售或回購決策會因政治上難以接受的殖利率水準而調整，即使單次操作可支撐債券價格，他們仍可能要求供給路徑不確定性的補償。

以一個月來看，殖利率曲線仍反映這項未解壓力。即使週一上漲，30年期殖利率仍較一個月前高6.8個基點，2年期則低9.9個基點；同期2年與30年期利差仍擴大16.7個基點。現金支應的回購或可中斷曲線陡峭化，但截至收盤，尚無證據顯示此舉已取代背後的財政、通膨與發債力量。

## 貿易衝擊使成長與通膨風險分流

最新一輪貿易升級中，加拿大主權債市的反應最為明顯。與華盛頓的談判破裂後，加幣一度下跌0.7%，至每美元兌C$1.3851；加拿大2年期與10年期公債殖利率則各自最多下跌9個基點，分別降至2.95%及3.68%。

債券上漲反映成長前景轉差。上週五稍晚談判失敗後，美國對數百項加拿大產品徵收的50%關稅生效；加拿大總理Mark Carney表示，加拿大將於9月8日對約$200億美國商品加徵報復性關稅。若相關措施持續，不僅威脅投資人原先預期未來數月出現的經濟回升，估計也可能危及9萬個加拿大工作機會。

市場因而把截至明年7月所反映的加拿大升息幅度，從上週五的75個基點降至65個基點。這項重新定價不表示關稅在所有層面都會壓低通膨：報復性關稅可能推高個別商品價格、擾亂供應鏈並削弱匯率。但就加拿大利率而言，市場眼前的判斷是，在央行反應函數中，產出與投資損失的影響將大於價格效應。

美國與伊朗相關的宣布則呈現不同的風險組合。Bessent揚言單方面懲罰持續與德黑蘭交易的國家，並表示總統Donald Trump正聯絡外國領袖，提出具體要求與期限。政府並未說明將針對哪些國家、企業、交易或制裁，因此這項行動能否實質限制伊朗出口、航運、保險或支付，仍不明朗。

細節不足使油價得以維持跌勢。伊朗對亞洲的出貨量此前已大幅下降，原油價格仍包含可觀的戰爭溢價，但週一的宣布並未證實實體供給將進一步減少。因此，WTI與布蘭特原油下跌支撐美債，二級制裁的威脅則保留了通膨壓力再起的可能性。

風險集中於實際執行。若措施針對中國或其他大型買方，可能減少可用供給，卻也會引發另一場可能推升美國進口價格的貿易衝突；若主要停留在警告層次，對石油流向的影響可能小得多。週一美債上漲，反映的是收盤前已知的結果，也就是原油下跌且沒有詳細執法方案，而不是市場相信地緣政治通膨風險已經結束。

德國財政部長Lars Klingbeil指出，這項風險已廣泛浮現。他把全球債券殖利率上升與歐洲天然氣成本提高歸因於伊朗戰爭。這項判斷無法解釋週一美債為何上漲，卻凸顯單日原油下跌不足以決定長天期債券前景：能源供應受擾之際，多個主要市場也正面臨創紀錄的主權舉債與異常龐大的企業發債。

## 信用需求創高，AI或有槓桿浮現

進入8月最後階段，美國投資級債券的供給與需求雙雙創下紀錄。距月底仍有兩週，藍籌企業借款人已發行$1,570億債券，連續第三個月改寫單月發行紀錄。市場對9月發行量的預估介於$1,750億至$2,500億，兩端相差$750億，使投資組合經理人難以判斷需要消化多少供給。

目前需求仍足以避免龐大發行量造成全面性干擾。JPMorgan Asset Management投資組合經理Kelsey Berro引用的資金流資料顯示，散戶今年買進投資級債券的金額，已超過自2010年以來任何一個完整年度。信用債經理人告訴她，即使9月供給達$2,500億仍可消化；她也預期，若發債日程告一段落而利差沒有擴大，場外觀望的買方會迅速回流。

這份需求能否持續格外重要，因為AI投資週期不僅擴大一般債券供給，也增加了未以傳統債務形式列在提供支援之科技公司帳上的義務。今年企業為資料中心及相關AI投資已借款逾$4,100億。部分專案雖符合投資級評等條件，仍需高收益債投資人參與，原因是其施工、承租人與融資風險要求的殖利率高於傳統藍籌企業債。

Broadcom是目前最明確的例子，顯示投資人開始要求或有曝險的補償。其票息5.15%、2031年到期債券的殖利率在8月上升約14個基點，5年期信用違約交換保障成本則增加28個基點，升幅超過Oracle或SpaceX。

這次重新定價發生在市場討論一項逾$600億的AI晶片融資之後，Anthropic及其他客戶將從中受益。Broadcom可能為部分優先擔保級別提供保證。這類支援可降低專案或特殊目的載體的借款成本，但若客戶、擔保品或租賃付款未達預期，部分下行風險便會轉移至Broadcom。

這項機制不限於一筆擬議交易。晶片製造商及其他科技公司日益透過擔保、採購承諾、租賃與殘值支援，協助客戶取得資金。這些安排可讓形式上的借款實體與贊助企業分離，但若AI週期轉弱，仍可能對贊助企業形成請求權。JPMorgan策略師Tarek Hamid形容，累積的承諾正成為該產業底下一層日益增厚的槓桿。

Broadcom信用價格的變動屬個別公司情況，並不表示AI融資管道普遍關閉。投資級債券基金週一小幅上漲，創紀錄的初級市場供給也持續獲得創紀錄需求承接。關鍵差異在於能否取得資金與融資定價：資金仍然可得，但投資人正更明確區分單純的優先債務，以及可能把龐大或有負債重新帶回保證人資產負債表的結構。

SoftBank Group則尋求另一種資金來源。公司計畫發行¥1兆、折合$63億的7年期零售債，將是日本發行人歷來規模最大的個人投資者債券。預計9月4日定價，參考票息區間為4.3%至4.9%。

SoftBank擬將¥4,000億用於償還9月到期的零售債，其餘資金投入AI投資策略。公司已承諾向OpenAI投資逾$600億，也在擴大資料中心投資。這次發行接續4月的¥4,180億及6月的¥2,600億零售債，將是公司今年第三筆同類交易。

SoftBank依賴家庭投資人，既反映票息水準，也反映其信用狀況。日本信用評等機構預計給予該債券A評等；S&P則給予SoftBank BB+評等，較投資級低一級，展望穩定。銀行面臨存款成長疲弱，可能不願承擔相關評等與存續期間風險，因此零售投資人成為配售核心。Bloomberg Intelligence分析師Sharon Chen預期，票息將接近區間上端；她估計完成交易後，SoftBank的資金缺口仍將超過$200億，進一步提高其增發境外債券的可能性。

在科技信用市場壓力較大的一端，Ivanti的營運惡化顯示，當經常性收入成長不足以支應既有高槓桿資本結構時，後果會如何。第2季營收較上年同期下降11%至$1.89億，備考調整後獲利下滑21%至$7,200萬，年度經常性收入則減少1%至$7.78億。

訂閱及軟體即服務收入約占經常性收入的83%，並成長10%，但總額約5%來自正逐步淘汰的產品。公司不僅必須取代日益減少的舊產品銷售，每年還要支付約$2.8億利息。業績公布後，Ivanti一筆$18億、2029年到期的第一順位定期貸款下跌約8點，至每$1面額約報$0.36。

S&P於6月把Ivanti降至CCC，理由包括資本結構無法維持、現金持續流失，以及違約或進行困境換債的可能性升高。公司去年與貸款人達成協議，籌得$3.5億並延長到期日，為轉向訂閱制爭取時間。週一數據顯示，要使這次展期得以長久維持所需的營運改善仍未出現。

## 本地政策調整使部分新興市場受惠

土耳其央行比經濟學家預期更早取消緊急融資溢價，帶動當日幅度最大的利率變動之一。央行表示，將恢復以37%政策利率進行1週附買回標售，不再使用3月初因伊朗戰爭不確定性升高而採用的40%隔夜利率。

土耳其公債隨之上漲，2年期殖利率下降58個基點，10年期下降25個基點。較便宜的附買回融資可改善淨利差，銀行股一度上漲4.1%。市場原先普遍預期，這項決定要到9月10日政策會議後才會出現，因此提前實施引發揣測，認為成長疲弱在央行反應函數中的影響力正在上升。

這項調整不等於調降政策利率。基準利率仍為37%，7月通膨率也高達31.8%。央行近期把年底通膨預測從26%上調至28%，其市場參與者調查的預期則為29%。不過，融資操作正常化確實移除了實質上的3個百分點溢價；若價格壓力持續減輕，降息路徑也將更清楚。

印尼債市受惠於相反的政策組合：先前緊縮已使匯率趨穩，足以吸引外資回流。全球基金上週四淨買進$6.567億政府債券，創2019年7月以來最大單日流入。8月淨買進額達$9.3174億，使市場可望連續第三個月錄得資金流入。

印尼央行今年累計升息100個基點，最近一次會議維持利率不變，印尼盾8月因而升值1.8%。央行也擴大避險獎勵措施，並表示將把SRBI證券標售頻率從每週一次降為每兩週一次。這些措施旨在不立即再次升息的情況下，同時支撐外資需求與國內流動性。

初級市場需求也顯示情況改善。一次政府標售的投標金額達目標規模2.65倍，為去年12月以來最高。外資投標達17.2兆印尼盾，超過今年平均8.3兆印尼盾的2倍，並創2026年最高參與額。10年期殖利率已較6月高點下降52個基點，5年期下降69個基點，顯示即使殖利率優勢縮小，匯率穩定的影響仍更為顯著。

墨西哥數據支持長時間維持利率不變，而非重新緊縮或立即恢復寬鬆。第2季GDP較前一季成長1.4%，從修正後萎縮0.3%反彈，但略低於先前估計的1.5%。營建業成長4.8%，服務業成長2.3%，顯示復甦並非只由出口改善帶動。

通膨訊號好壞不一。8月上半月整體物價較上年同期上漲3.26%，高於前一個半月期的3.14%；核心通膨則從3.95%微降至3.93%。墨西哥央行月初維持6.5%政策利率，並稱此水準適當。成長復甦已足以避免央行被迫降息，但服務通膨，以及能源和美國貿易政策的不確定性，仍限制寬鬆空間。

巴基斯坦與尚比亞的主權信用發展均偏正面，但原因不同。Moody’s把巴基斯坦評等由Caa1調升至B3，展望穩定，理由是外匯存底增加、財政指標改善及國內融資成本下降。外匯存底已達$171億，評等調升後，多數美元債券上漲。

這次升評使巴基斯坦由極高信用風險降至高信用風險，但並未消除其脆弱性。Moody’s仍指出，該國外部財務薄弱、債務負擔能力不佳，且稅收基礎狹窄。巴基斯坦依賴燃料進口，仍容易受到能源衝擊，評等也依然屬於投機級。其意義在於，持續穩定已使韌性改善，得以再向遠離2023年近乎違約的狀態邁進一步。

尚比亞在8月13日大選後首次舉行本幣債券標售，投標金額較發行的63億克瓦查高出37%。7年期債券需求最強，殖利率較6月標售下降101個基點至14.79%。這與6月投標不足以覆蓋發行額的情況形成對比。

投資人把需求增強與總統Hakainde Hichilema連任，以及財政整頓可望延續相連結。反對派領袖Brian Mundubile仍質疑選舉結果，並打算向憲法法院提出挑戰。儘管如此，這次標售顯示，現有投資人願意給予較低的近期政治風險溢價。尚比亞本地債今年報酬約37%，相較之下，較廣泛的新興市場本幣債指數報酬約為4%。

## 債務重整由期限壓力邁向實際執行

Braskem跨過了前一週結束時仍未解決的關鍵門檻。據《聖保羅州報》報導，這家巴西石化生產商已取得足夠主要債權人支持，可啟動庭外重整。公司原先尋求在週一緊急保護措施屆滿前，獲得至少三分之一債權人的同意。

提出申請後，各方有90天敲定涵蓋近$110億債務的條款。這是實質性的狀態改變：公司不再只是面對一系列不具約束力的方案與即將到期的暫緩措施，而是已有一條通往具約束力協議的明確路徑。

重要條款仍未定案。包括Elliott Investment Management與Contrarian Capital Management在內的債權人，已要求Petrobras挹注股本、營運資金或次順位債務。今年稍早，IG4 Capital收購以Novonor持股作擔保的不良貸款，並與Petrobras共同取得控制權，Braskem的控制結構因而改變。這家國營石油公司是否願意提供資本或改善商業付款條件，將影響現有債權人最終可保留多少價值。

庭外程序的設計，是要比司法重整更快速、對營運干擾更小。足夠數量的貸款人核准最終條款後，法官便可批准協議，使更廣泛的債權人群體受到約束。若各方未能在90天內完成交易，Braskem仍可能必須尋求破產保護。因此，跨過支持門檻可避免局勢立即惡化，卻尚未決定回收率、擔保品分配或股東支援的規模。

龍光集團則更進一步進入執行階段。香港法院批准這家中國開發商的重整方案，使獲多數債權人支持的計畫得以自8月21日起生效。龍光約有$75億境外債務需要重整，自2022年違約後，與債權人的談判已歷時逾四年。

法院批准解決了一項重大程序障礙，卻無法修復營運環境。中國7月新屋價格跌勢加快，其他開發商也在完成第一輪重整後再度遭遇流動性問題。龍光如今必須在房屋銷售疲弱、專案仍有融資需求的環境下，落實償債計畫。

這項法律進展仍有實質意義。債權人曾於2022年對龍光兩家子公司提出清盤呈請；隨重整談判推進，呈請在2024年初遭到駁回。其後談判又持續兩年，部分原因是香港一項豪宅地產的再融資遇到困難。8月21日的生效日，使漫長談判轉化為可實際執行的計畫；不過，未來現金產生能力仍將決定公司能否避免再次重整。

## 後續市場意義

8月26日公布的7月個人消費支出（PCE）通膨，將檢驗週一由實質殖利率帶動的漲勢，能否承受有關聯準會反應函數的新資訊。經濟學家預期，整體通膨率將由3.7%降至3.6%，核心通膨率維持3.3%。核心物價月增率預計為0.2%，高於6月的0.1%，仍符合逐步通膨降溫；若價格更廣泛加速，幾乎未變的4.234% 2年期殖利率將受到挑戰，曲線前端也會再度承壓。

數據組成格外重要，因為週一美債行情幾乎完全由實質殖利率推動。即使油價下跌，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅微幅下降，顯示投資人並未因單日能源價格轉弱，便大幅下調中期通膨補償。溫和的基礎價格與消費增幅可為較低殖利率提供經濟面支撐；若服務通膨較強，這波漲勢將繼續依賴Bessent尚未認可的債務管理預期。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh於8月28日首次發表Jackson Hole主題演說，是更重要的政策事件。投資人希望他能更清楚說明，如何權衡居高不下的通膨、部分需求轉弱及長期借款成本上升。他在7月會議後提供的指引有限，已加劇市場波動；決策委員會內既有主張升息的官員，也有人願意等待通膨降溫。

財政部擴大後的回購計畫將於9月9日啟動。首批操作會確立實際規模及合格券種，但是否動用TGA仍須另作決定。下一次季度再融資安排公布前，例行標售仍是明定政策。供給面的效益不只取決於財政部買回多少舊券，也取決於日後是否必須透過國庫券或附息債券重建現金餘額。

加拿大9月8日實施的報復性關稅，以及美國對伊朗行動尚未明定的時程，形成性質不同的通膨與成長考驗。加拿大債券市場正反映更嚴重的經濟損害及較少的升息，美債則受惠於原油下跌。若報復性關稅升級，或對伊朗石油主要買方的制裁確實生效，進口或能源成本上升可能逆轉部分利多。

日本9月1日的10年期公債標售及9月3日的30年期標售，將在日本央行9月18日決策前，檢驗全球對長天期債券的需求。日本央行前審議委員足立誠司預期9月升息，最快1月再升一次；交換市場則認為下一步行動的機率約為80%。日圓約報每美元159.20，7月核心通膨加速至1.8%，但第2季個人消費較上年同期下降0.1%。若標售疲弱，日本殖利率可能上升並把壓力傳導至美債；需求穩健則表示，即使市場預期政策緊縮，目前的價格讓利已經足夠。

SoftBank於9月4日定價，將衡量日本家庭投資人要求多少報酬，才願意為一家非投資級公司的再融資及AI承諾提供資金。若票息落在4.3%至4.9%區間上端附近，代表公司仍可取得融資，但這筆創紀錄交易需要異常高的票息。若其後再發行境外債券，將顯示公司如何處理剩餘資金缺口。

Broadcom最終提供的擔保、債權順位與融資金額，則會從另一角度檢驗AI信用風險。其債券殖利率與CDS上升，顯示投資人已開始為專案支援可能回到企業資產負債表的風險收費。最終條款將決定這次重新定價是否僅限單一發行人，或擴散至其他使用擔保、租賃與採購承諾的科技公司。

9月投資級債券發行日程，接著將檢驗創紀錄需求是否深到足以消化$1,750億至$2,500億預估區間上端的供給。當美債殖利率下降、散戶資金持續流入時，龐大供給仍可與緊俏的信用條件並存。若政府公債殖利率再度上升，並遇上更多AI相關借款，投資人將要求更高利差或更高的整體票息。

Braskem的90天談判及龍光的計畫執行，仍是個別公司的落實考驗。Braskem尚須敲定條款、取得資本並獲債權人批准；龍光則必須產生足夠營運現金流，履行法院批准的計畫。兩者進展取決於契約支援與資產價值，而非廣泛信用債基金當日的小幅上漲。

綜觀這些事件，核心問題是週一長天期殖利率下跌能否獲得經濟面的確認。油價下降及可能以現金支應的回購均有利於長天期債券，但兩者都不代表聯邦政府的籌資需求永久減少。PCE數據與Warsh的政策訊號可驗證實質殖利率下降是否合理，財政部9月操作則可改變供給結構。若這些管道無法形成持久支撐，長端仍將暴露於財政舉債、全球債券供給及企業不斷擴大的資金需求之下。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌與現金支應回購的期待支撐美債長端，殖利率曲線隨漲勢趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
8月24日美國公債上漲，殖利率曲線趨平。2年期殖利率微降0.3個基點至4.234%，5年期下降2.3個基點至4.402%，10年期下跌3.7個基點至4.698%，30年期則下降4.5個基點至5.227%。10年期實質殖利率下跌3.4個基點，幾乎解釋全部名目殖利率變動；損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.3個基點，顯示市場調低的是所要求的實質殖利率，而非認定中期通膨前景已明顯改善。

即使美國財政部長Scott Bessent揚言懲罰持續與伊朗交易的國家，WTI仍下跌2.16%，布蘭特原油下跌2.39%，為債市提供眼前的利多。這項宣布缺乏執行細節，也未證實實體供給將進一步減少。另有報導稱，官員正考慮動用財政部$9,350億現金餘額的一部分，買回票息較高的舊券，可能延後原本為支應回購而必須增發的國庫券，美債因此進一步上漲。

Bessent表示，擴大後的計畫尚未買進任何債券，例行標售將會持續，且11月初公布季度再融資安排前不會有所改變。因此，收盤行情反映的是一種可能更有利的籌資方式，而非動用現金的承諾或聯邦借款需求永久減少。黃金上漲2.47%；美元指數當日上升0.18%，但全週仍下跌0.66%。信用債基金小幅走高，標普500指數則下跌0.28%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.97%，半導體股下挫2.70%，反映投資人重新評估AI投資熱潮帶來的融資負擔。
overall_summary.summary: 原油下跌，加上財政部可能動用現金餘額支應長債回購的報導，帶動中長天期殖利率走低；但損益兩平通膨率幾乎未變，政策也尚無承諾，這波漲勢能否持續仍未明朗。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on Aug. 24 as lower oil prices reduced immediate inflation pressure and a report that the government could use its cash balance to finance repurchases offered a more favorable interpretation of the expanded long-bond buyback program. The move was concentrated in intermediate and long maturities: the 2-year yield slipped 0.3 basis point to 4.234%, the 5-year fell 2.3 basis points to 4.402%, the 10-year declined 3.7 basis points to 4.698% and the 30-year dropped 4.5 basis points to 5.227%.

The rally flattened the curve and reversed part of Friday’s activity-driven selloff. The 2s10s spread narrowed 3.4 basis points to 46.4 basis points, while 2s30s compressed 4.2 basis points to 99.3 basis points. The 10-year real yield accounted for almost the entire nominal move, falling 3.4 basis points to 2.368%, while the 10-year breakeven eased only 0.3 basis point to 2.33%. Investors therefore marked down the real yield required to hold Treasuries without concluding that the medium-term inflation outlook had materially improved.

Oil provided a cleaner disinflationary impulse. WTI fell 2.16% to $85.18 and Brent lost 2.39% to $92.13 even after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened penalties against countries that continue doing business with Iran. His “economic D-Day” announcement supplied few operational details, and crude retained its decline. The price move offered bonds relief from the energy pressure that had recently pushed inflation compensation and global yields higher.

The other support came from a report that Treasury officials were considering using part of the department’s $935 billion cash balance to buy higher-coupon older securities. Drawing on cash would avoid immediately issuing bills to finance every repurchase, making the near-term supply effect more supportive of longer maturities than a simple exchange of long debt for short debt. Treasuries extended their gains after the report, taking the 10-year yield to about 4.69% during the New York afternoon.

Bessent stopped short of adopting the idea. He said no bonds had yet been bought under the expanded program, affirmed that regular auctions would continue and indicated that changes would not come before the quarterly refunding announcement at the start of November. The session was therefore a repricing of a possible funding method, not evidence that Treasury had committed additional cash or reduced its future borrowing requirement.

That distinction remained visible outside the rates market. Gold futures rose 2.47% to $4,738.20 and were up 7.25% over one week, while the Dollar Index gained 0.18% on the day but remained 0.66% lower over the week. Long Treasuries benefited from the prospect of fewer offsetting bills, yet demand for an alternative to dollar assets continued as investors assessed whether repeated intervention in bond yields could ultimately transfer pressure into the currency.

Credit markets were steadier than equities. Investment-grade and high-yield bond funds edged higher, while the S&P 500 fell 0.28% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.97%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 2.70%, extending its weekly fall to 9.49%, as Nvidia’s earnings approached and investors reassessed the financing burden surrounding the artificial-intelligence investment boom. The Treasury rally lowered the benchmark rate for borrowers, but it did not remove the corporate supply or contingent liabilities competing with the government for capital.

## Cash-Funded Buybacks Remain a Possibility, Not Policy

The Treasury General Account report mattered because it changed the possible sequencing of the buybacks announced the previous week. Dealers had generally expected repurchases of older 10- to 30-year securities to be financed through additional bill issuance. That approach would remove duration from private portfolios but leave the total amount of debt in the market essentially unchanged, replacing longer obligations with securities that mature in no more than a year.

Using cash would postpone that offset. The TGA held $935 billion on Aug. 20, and Morgan Stanley estimated that Treasury might have between $80 billion and $200 billion available depending on how it defined excess cash. Even the low end would be far larger than the scheduled long-maturity buybacks: Treasury’s calendar permits as much as $14 billion of operations in 10- to 30-year securities between Sept. 9 and Nov. 4 after the department said it would at least double liquidity-support purchases.

The headline balance is not equivalent to money available for discretionary market support. Treasury keeps cash at the Federal Reserve to meet expenditures ranging from benefits to payments for employees and contractors. Its policy since 2015 has been to maintain at least five days of spending or $150 billion as protection against a disruption that prevents access to debt markets. Rising cyber risks and uncertain daily outlays strengthen the argument for a substantial buffer.

Using the TGA would also shift financing through time rather than eliminate it. Cash spent on repurchases would eventually need to be rebuilt through taxes, lower expenditures or future borrowing. The immediate benefit would be less simultaneous issuance while Treasury removes duration; the later consequence would depend on how and when the balance was replenished. That is why the market could rally on the report without treating the $935 billion as a permanent reduction in supply.

Bessent preserved that uncertainty at his press conference. He said Treasury would continue its regular auction program and gave no indication that coupon sizes would be reduced. He also said no purchases had yet occurred under the new initiative, which begins Sept. 9. The next quarterly refunding at the start of November remains the formal point at which Treasury would ordinarily announce material changes to auction, buyback or cash-management policy.

The absence of a new commitment did not erase the session’s move because funding mechanics matter at the margin. The 10-year yield was about 4 basis points lower at 4.69% after the cash report, near its eventual daily level. The 30-year outperformed the 2-year, and the 2s30s curve flattened, consistent with investors assigning some probability to a more favorable long-end supply mix.

The scale of trading showed that the adjustment was not confined to an inactive market. FINRA recorded $1.073 trillion of Treasury par activity, 9.5% more than Friday. Nominal-coupon activity rose 4.7% to $871.3 billion. Turnover in maturities beyond 20 years increased 21.6% to $107.6 billion, while activity in the greater-than-10-year through 20-year sector climbed 28.4% to $82.8 billion. The data do not reveal whether customers were net buyers or sellers, but the long-end rally occurred alongside increased transaction volume.

The argument for intervention nevertheless remains contested. Goldman Sachs strategists said larger buybacks do not address the fiscal and inflation forces responsible for the rise in long yields and are unlikely to reset rate levels materially even if expanded. Wells Fargo identified slower growth and inflation, clearer Fed policy, fiscal consolidation or reduced investment-grade issuance as the kinds of catalysts that could produce a more durable decline.

Market-functioning evidence also complicates Treasury’s stated liquidity rationale. JPMorgan research found that depth in longer-maturity Treasuries improved about 38% during the first three months of 2026, helped by both existing buybacks and a changing buyer base that includes more high-frequency traders. Swap spreads and rate volatility were not showing exceptional dysfunction when Treasury enlarged the program. The policy can still improve liquidity in individual older securities, but the timing has encouraged investors to view it as a response to the absolute level of yields.

That interpretation creates a potential term-premium cost. Sudden changes made two weeks after a quarterly schedule reduce the predictability normally associated with Treasury debt management. If investors expect future auction or buyback decisions to react to politically uncomfortable yields, they may demand compensation for uncertainty about the supply path even as an individual operation supports prices.

The monthly curve still reflects that unresolved pressure. Despite Monday’s rally, the 30-year yield was 6.8 basis points higher than one month earlier, while the 2-year was 9.9 basis points lower. The 2s30s spread remained 16.7 basis points wider over that period. Cash-funded repurchases could interrupt the steepening, but the completed close did not establish that they had displaced the fiscal, inflation and issuance forces behind it.

## Trade Shocks Split Growth Risk From Inflation Risk

Canada supplied the clearest sovereign-rates response to the latest trade escalation. The Canadian dollar fell as much as 0.7% to C$1.3851 per US dollar after negotiations with Washington collapsed, while 2- and 10-year Canadian government yields each declined as much as 9 basis points, to 2.95% and 3.68% respectively.

The bond rally reflected a worsening growth outlook. US tariffs of 50% took effect on hundreds of Canadian products after the talks failed late Friday, and Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada would impose counter-tariffs on about $20 billion of US goods on Sept. 8. The measures threaten the economic pickup investors had expected in the coming months and could put an estimated 90,000 Canadian jobs at risk if they persist.

Markets consequently reduced the amount of Canadian tightening priced through July to 65 basis points from 75 basis points on Friday. The repricing did not mean tariffs are disinflationary in every respect: retaliatory duties can raise individual prices, disrupt supply chains and weaken the currency. For Canadian rates, however, the immediate judgment was that lost output and investment would outweigh the price effect in the central bank’s reaction function.

The US-Iran announcement produced a different balance of risks. Bessent threatened unilateral punishment against countries that continue trading with Tehran and said President Donald Trump was contacting foreign leaders with specific requests and deadlines. The administration did not identify the countries, companies, transactions or sanctions that would be targeted, leaving uncertain whether the campaign would materially restrict Iranian exports, shipping, insurance or payments.

That lack of detail helped oil retain its decline. Iranian shipments to Asia had already fallen sharply, and crude prices still carried a substantial war premium, but Monday’s announcement did not establish an additional physical supply loss. Lower WTI and Brent prices therefore supported Treasuries even as the threat of secondary sanctions preserved the possibility of renewed inflation pressure.

The risk is concentrated in implementation. Measures aimed at China or other large buyers could reduce available supply but would also open another trade confrontation capable of raising US import prices. Measures that rely primarily on warnings may have much less effect on oil flows. Monday’s Treasury rally reflected the outcome visible by the close—lower crude and no detailed enforcement package—rather than confidence that the geopolitical inflation risk had ended.

Germany’s finance minister, Lars Klingbeil, underscored how widely that risk is already being felt. He attributed the rise in global bond yields and Europe’s higher gas costs to the Iran war. His assessment did not explain Monday’s US rally, but it highlighted why a single decline in crude cannot settle the duration outlook: energy disruption is operating alongside record sovereign borrowing and unusually heavy corporate issuance across several major markets.

## Record Credit Demand Meets AI Contingent Leverage

US investment-grade issuance entered the final part of August with both supply and demand at records. Blue-chip borrowers had sold $157 billion with two weeks remaining in the month, already producing a third consecutive monthly issuance record. September estimates ranged from $175 billion to $250 billion, a $75 billion gap that leaves portfolio managers uncertain about how much inventory they will need to absorb.

Demand has so far prevented that volume from producing broad disruption. Retail purchases of investment-grade bonds have already exceeded the full-year total in every year going back to 2010, according to flow data cited by JPMorgan Asset Management portfolio manager Kelsey Berro. Credit managers told her that even $250 billion of September supply was manageable, and she expected sidelined buyers to return quickly if the calendar cleared without wider spreads.

The durability of that demand matters because the AI investment cycle is expanding both ordinary bond supply and obligations that do not appear as conventional debt at the technology companies providing support. Companies have borrowed more than $410 billion this year for data centers and related AI investment. Some projects that qualify for investment-grade ratings have still needed high-yield investors because their construction, tenant and financing risks require yields above those available on conventional blue-chip debt.

Broadcom offered the clearest current sign that investors are beginning to charge for contingent exposure. The yield on its 5.15% bond due in 2031 rose about 14 basis points during August, while the price of 5-year credit-default protection increased 28 basis points, a larger move than for Oracle or SpaceX.

The repricing followed discussions about more than $60 billion of financing for AI chips benefiting Anthropic and other customers. Broadcom could guarantee part of a senior-secured tranche. Such support can lower the borrowing cost for the project or special-purpose vehicle, but it transfers some downside to Broadcom if customers, collateral or lease payments fail to perform.

That mechanism extends beyond one proposed transaction. Chipmakers and other technology companies have increasingly used guarantees, purchase commitments, leases and residual-value support to strengthen customers’ access to capital. Those arrangements can keep a formal borrowing entity separate from the sponsor while still creating a claim on the sponsor if the AI cycle weakens. JPMorgan strategist Tarek Hamid described the accumulated commitments as a growing layer of leverage beneath the sector.

Broadcom’s credit move was company-specific rather than evidence of a generalized closure of AI financing. Investment-grade funds gained modestly on Monday, and record primary supply continued to meet record demand. The distinction is between access and price: financing remains available, but investors are differentiating more sharply between straightforward senior debt and structures that can bring large contingent liabilities back onto a guarantor’s balance sheet.

SoftBank Group is pursuing a different source of funding. The company plans a ¥1 trillion, or $6.3 billion, 7-year retail bond, the largest sale to individuals by any Japanese issuer. Pricing is expected on Sept. 4 within an indicative coupon range of 4.3% to 4.9%.

SoftBank intends to use ¥400 billion to refinance retail bonds maturing in September and the remainder to support its AI investment strategy. It has committed more than $60 billion to OpenAI and is expanding data-center investment. The new offering follows ¥418 billion of retail issuance in April and ¥260 billion in June, making it the company’s third such transaction this year.

The reliance on households reflects both the coupon and the credit. Japan Credit Rating Agency is expected to assign the bonds an A rating, while S&P rates SoftBank BB+, one notch below investment grade, with a stable outlook. Banks face weak deposit growth and may be reluctant to assume the rating and duration risk, leaving retail investors central to distribution. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Sharon Chen expects pricing near the upper end of the range and estimates that SoftBank will still face a funding shortfall exceeding $20 billion after the deal, increasing the likelihood of additional offshore issuance.

At the stressed end of technology credit, Ivanti’s operating decline showed what happens when recurring revenue does not grow quickly enough to service an already leveraged capital structure. Q2 revenue fell 11% from a year earlier to $189 million, while pro-forma adjusted earnings declined 21% to $72 million. Annual recurring revenue slipped 1% to $778 million.

Subscription and software-as-a-service revenue accounted for about 83% of recurring revenue and was growing 10%, but roughly 5% of the total came from products being phased out. That leaves the company needing to replace declining legacy sales while paying about $280 million of annual interest. Ivanti’s $1.8 billion first-lien term loan due in 2029 fell about 8 points after the results to roughly 36 cents on the dollar.

S&P cut Ivanti to CCC in June, citing an unsustainable capital structure, persistent cash burn and an increased likelihood of default or a distressed exchange. The company raised $350 million and extended maturities in a lender agreement last year, buying time for the subscription transition. Monday’s figures showed that the operational improvement required to make that extension durable had not yet arrived.

## Local Policy Changes Reward Selected Emerging Markets

Turkey’s central bank delivered one of the largest rates moves of the day by removing an emergency funding premium earlier than economists expected. The bank said it would resume 1-week repo auctions at its 37% policy rate, reversing the use of the 40% overnight rate introduced in early March as uncertainty from the Iran war intensified.

Turkish government bonds rallied, with 2-year yields falling 58 basis points and 10-year yields declining 25 basis points. Bank shares gained as much as 4.1% because cheaper repo funding should improve net interest margins. The decision was widely expected only after the Sept. 10 policy meeting, so its timing encouraged speculation that concerns about weak growth were becoming more influential in the reaction function.

The change did not amount to a policy-rate cut. The benchmark remained 37%, and inflation was still 31.8% in July. The central bank recently raised its year-end inflation projection to 28% from 26%, while its survey of market participants showed a 29% expectation. The funding normalization nevertheless removed the effective 3-percentage-point premium and created a clearer path toward rate cuts if price pressure continues to ease.

Indonesia’s bond market benefited from the opposite policy mix: earlier tightening had stabilized the currency enough to draw foreign buyers back. Global funds bought a net $656.7 million of government debt on Thursday, the largest daily inflow since July 2019. Net purchases for August reached $931.74 million, putting the market on course for a third consecutive month of inflows.

The rupiah had gained 1.8% during August after Bank Indonesia raised rates by a cumulative 100 basis points this year and held at its latest meeting. The central bank also expanded a hedging incentive and said it would reduce auctions of its SRBI securities from weekly to every two weeks. Those measures are intended to support foreign demand and domestic liquidity without another immediate policy increase.

The improvement was visible in primary demand. A government auction produced bids equal to 2.65 times the target, the strongest ratio since December. Foreign bids reached 17.2 trillion rupiah, more than double this year’s 8.3 trillion rupiah average and the highest participation of 2026. The 10-year yield had fallen 52 basis points from its June peak and the 5-year 69 basis points, showing how currency stabilization can outweigh a narrowing yield advantage.

Mexico’s data supported a prolonged rate hold rather than either renewed tightening or an immediate return to easing. GDP expanded 1.4% in Q2 from the previous quarter, rebounding from a revised 0.3% contraction but falling just short of the earlier 1.5% estimate. Construction rose 4.8% and services grew 2.3%, making the recovery broader than an export-only improvement.

Inflation presented a mixed picture. Headline prices rose 3.26% in the first half of August from a year earlier, up from 3.14% in the prior two-week period, while core inflation edged down to 3.93% from 3.95%. Banxico kept its policy rate at 6.5% earlier in the month and described that level as appropriate. Growth has recovered enough to avoid forcing a cut, while services inflation and uncertainty surrounding energy and US trade policy limit room to ease.

Sovereign-credit developments were favorable in Pakistan and Zambia, though for different reasons. Moody’s raised Pakistan to B3 from Caa1 with a stable outlook, citing higher foreign-exchange reserves, better fiscal metrics and lower domestic financing costs. Reserves had reached $17.1 billion, and most dollar bonds gained after the rating action.

The upgrade moves Pakistan from very high to high credit risk but does not remove its vulnerabilities. Moody’s still identified fragile external finances, weak debt affordability and a narrow revenue base. The country remains exposed to an energy shock because it imports fuel, and the rating is still speculative grade. The significance is that sustained stabilization has improved resilience enough to support another step away from the near-default conditions of 2023.

Zambia’s first local-currency bond auction since the Aug. 13 election attracted bids 37% above the 6.3 billion kwacha offered. The 7-year bond drew the strongest interest, with its yield falling 101 basis points from the June auction to 14.79%. The result contrasted with the June sale, when bids failed to cover the amount offered.

Investors associated the stronger demand with President Hakainde Hichilema’s reelection and expectations of continued fiscal consolidation. The political outcome is still disputed by opposition leader Brian Mundubile, who intended to challenge it in the Constitutional Court. The auction nonetheless showed that current investors were willing to assign a lower near-term political premium: Zambia’s local debt has returned about 37% this year, compared with roughly 4% for a broader emerging-market local-currency index.

## Restructurings Advance From Deadlines to Execution

Braskem crossed the immediate threshold that had remained unresolved at the end of the previous week. The Brazilian petrochemical producer reached agreement with enough of its main creditors to begin an out-of-court restructuring, according to O Estado de São Paulo. It had been seeking support from at least one-third of creditors before the expiration of emergency protection on Monday.

The filing gives the parties 90 days to finalize terms covering nearly $11 billion of debt. That is a material change in status: the company now has a defined route toward a binding agreement rather than simply a collection of nonbinding proposals and an expiring standstill.

Important terms remain unsettled. Creditors including Elliott Investment Management and Contrarian Capital Management have pressed Petrobras to contribute equity, working capital or junior debt. Braskem’s controlling structure changed earlier this year when IG4 Capital acquired nonperforming loans secured by Novonor’s shares and took shared control alongside Petrobras. The state-controlled oil company’s willingness to supply capital or improve commercial payment terms will influence how much value remains for existing creditors.

The process is intended to be faster and less disruptive than judicial restructuring. Once sufficient lenders approve final terms, a judge can ratify the agreement and bind the wider creditor group. If the parties fail to complete the deal during the 90-day period, Braskem could still have to pursue bankruptcy protection. Reaching the threshold therefore prevents an immediate escalation without determining recoveries, collateral allocation or the size of any shareholder support.

Logan Group moved farther into implementation. A Hong Kong court sanctioned the Chinese developer’s restructuring, allowing a scheme supported by a majority of debt holders to take effect on Aug. 21. Logan had about $7.5 billion of offshore debt to restructure and had spent more than four years negotiating with creditors after its 2022 default.

Court approval resolves a major procedural obstacle but does not repair the operating environment. Chinese new-home prices fell at a faster pace in July, and other developers have encountered fresh liquidity problems after completing initial restructurings. Logan must now execute the repayment plan while dealing with weak property sales and the financing demands of its projects.

The legal advance is nonetheless meaningful. Creditors had filed winding-up petitions against two Logan units in 2022, and those petitions were dismissed in early 2024 as restructuring talks progressed. Negotiations then continued for another two years, partly because of refinancing difficulties connected to a luxury Hong Kong property. The Aug. 21 effective date turns that long negotiation into an operative plan, even though future cash generation will determine whether another restructuring can be avoided.

## Forward Market Significance

July personal-consumption-expenditure inflation on Aug. 26 will test whether Monday’s real-yield rally can survive fresh information about the Fed’s reaction function. Economists expect headline inflation to ease to 3.6% from 3.7% and core inflation to remain at 3.3%. The expected 0.2% monthly rise in core prices, after 0.1% in June, would be consistent with gradual disinflation; a broader acceleration would challenge the near-unchanged 4.234% 2-year yield and return pressure to the front of the curve.

The composition will matter because Monday’s Treasury move came almost entirely through real yields. The 10-year breakeven barely declined despite the fall in oil, suggesting investors did not use one softer energy session to reduce medium-term inflation compensation materially. Benign underlying prices and moderate consumption would provide economic support for lower yields. Firmer services inflation would leave the rally dependent on debt-management expectations that Bessent has not endorsed.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole keynote on Aug. 28 is the larger policy event. Investors are looking for a clearer account of how he weighs stubborn inflation, weaker parts of demand and the rise in long-term borrowing costs. His limited guidance after the July meeting contributed to volatility, and the committee includes both officials who favored a rate increase and others willing to wait for inflation to cool.

Treasury’s expanded buybacks begin Sept. 9. The first operations will establish their actual size and eligible securities, but any use of the TGA requires a separate decision. Regular auctions remain the stated policy through the next quarterly refunding. The supply benefit will depend not only on how much older debt Treasury buys but also on whether the cash balance later has to be rebuilt through bills or coupons.

Canada’s Sept. 8 counter-tariffs and the unspecified timeline in the Iran campaign create distinct inflation and growth tests. Canadian bonds are pricing greater economic damage and fewer rate increases, while US Treasuries benefited from lower crude. Escalating retaliatory duties or effective sanctions on Iranian oil buyers could reverse part of that relief by raising import or energy costs.

Japan’s 10-year government-bond auction on Sept. 1 and 30-year sale on Sept. 3 will test global demand for duration before the Bank of Japan’s Sept. 18 decision. A former BOJ board member, Seiji Adachi, expects a September increase and another as early as January, while swaps assign roughly an 80% probability to the next move. The yen was near 159.20 per dollar, and July core inflation accelerated to 1.8%, but personal consumption fell 0.1% from a year earlier in Q2. Weak auctions could raise Japanese yields and transmit pressure to Treasuries; solid demand would show that current concessions are sufficient despite tightening expectations.

SoftBank’s Sept. 4 pricing will measure how much Japanese households require to fund a below-investment-grade company’s refinancing and AI commitments. Placement near the upper end of the 4.3% to 4.9% range would preserve access while confirming that the record transaction needs an unusually large coupon. Further offshore issuance would reveal how the company addresses the remaining funding gap.

Broadcom’s eventual guarantee, seniority and financing amount will provide a separate test of AI credit risk. The rise in its bond yield and CDS shows that investors are already charging for the possibility that project support returns to the corporate balance sheet. Final terms will determine whether that repricing remains issuer-specific or spreads to other technology companies using guarantees, leases and purchase commitments.

The September investment-grade calendar will then show whether record demand is deep enough to absorb issuance at the high end of the $175 billion to $250 billion range. Heavy supply can coexist with tight credit conditions when Treasury yields fall and retail inflows remain strong. A renewed rise in government yields, combined with further AI borrowing, would force investors to demand more spread or higher all-in coupons.

Braskem’s 90-day negotiation and Logan’s implementation remain company-specific execution tests. Braskem still needs final terms, capital and creditor ratification; Logan needs operating cash flow sufficient to perform under its sanctioned plan. Their progress will depend on contractual support and asset values rather than the modest daily gain in broad credit funds.

Across these events, the central question is whether Monday’s decline in long yields receives economic confirmation. Lower oil and a possible cash-funded buyback supported duration, but neither represents a permanent reduction in the federal financing requirement. PCE and Warsh can validate lower real yields through the policy outlook; Treasury’s September operations can change the supply mix. Without one of those channels becoming durable, the long end remains exposed to fiscal borrowing, global bond supply and the expanding corporate demand for capital.

section_summaries.section_title: Cash-Funded Buybacks Remain a Possibility, Not Policy
section_summaries.summary: Using Treasury’s cash balance could postpone the issuance that would otherwise offset purchases of older 10- to 30-year securities. Estimates of potentially available cash ranged from $80 billion to $200 billion, compared with up to $14 billion of scheduled long-maturity buybacks from Sept. 9 through Nov. 4. Bessent made no commitment, affirmed regular auctions and left the start-of-November refunding as the formal decision point.

section_summaries.market_read: Canadian rates priced greater economic damage, while US duration responded to lower crude rather than an end to geopolitical inflation risk.
section_summaries.section_title: Trade Shocks Split Growth Risk From Inflation Risk
section_summaries.summary: Canadian yields and the currency fell after 50% US tariffs took effect and Canada scheduled counter-tariffs for Sept. 8, as markets judged the growth damage more important for monetary policy than the immediate price effect. In the US, lower crude supported Treasuries because the threatened campaign against Iran lacked enforcement details, though effective sanctions against major oil buyers could restore energy and import-price pressure.

section_summaries.market_read: Credit remained accessible, but pricing increasingly distinguished conventional senior debt from structures carrying contingent AI liabilities.
section_summaries.next_check: Broadcom’s final guarantee, seniority and financing amount will determine whether the repricing remains issuer-specific.
section_summaries.section_title: Record Credit Demand Meets AI Contingent Leverage
section_summaries.summary: Record demand continued to absorb record investment-grade issuance, but investors charged Broadcom more for possible guarantees tied to over $60 billion of AI-chip financing. Such guarantees, leases and purchase commitments can return project risk to a sponsor’s balance sheet. SoftBank planned a ¥1 trillion retail bond to refinance maturities and fund AI investment, while Ivanti’s weakening revenue and heavy interest burden pushed its first-lien loan sharply lower.

section_summaries.market_read: Currency stabilization and lower effective funding costs rewarded selected local markets even where formal policy rates did not fall.
section_summaries.section_title: Local Policy Changes Reward Selected Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: Turkey removed an emergency funding premium by restoring 1-week repo auctions at its 37% policy rate, driving a sharp government-bond rally without formally cutting rates. Indonesia drew its largest daily foreign government-debt inflow since 2019 after prior tightening stabilized the rupiah. Mexico’s growth and inflation mix supported a prolonged hold, while Pakistan’s upgrade and Zambia’s strongly covered post-election auction reflected improving but still qualified sovereign confidence.

section_summaries.next_check: Braskem must complete terms within 90 days, while Logan must generate enough operating cash to perform under its plan.
section_summaries.section_title: Restructurings Advance From Deadlines to Execution
section_summaries.summary: Braskem secured enough creditor support to begin an out-of-court restructuring and now has 90 days to finalize terms for nearly $11 billion of debt, though shareholder support and recoveries remain unsettled. A Hong Kong court sanctioned Logan Group’s restructuring, turning four years of negotiations over about $7.5 billion of offshore debt into an operative plan whose success still depends on cash generation amid weak property sales.

section_summaries.market_read: Without durable policy, inflation or supply support, long maturities remain exposed to fiscal borrowing and expanding corporate demand for capital.
section_summaries.summary: The durability of the long-end rally depends on economic confirmation or a lasting change in the supply mix. July PCE inflation and Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole keynote will test the case for lower real yields, while Treasury’s Sept. 9 buybacks will reveal the actual scale and eligible securities. Canadian retaliation or effective sanctions on Iranian oil buyers could restore inflation pressure through import and energy costs.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally and flatten as lower oil and cash-funded buyback hopes support the long end
overall_summary.session_narrative:
US Treasuries rallied and the curve flattened on Aug. 24. The 2-year yield slipped 0.3 basis point to 4.234%, the 5-year fell 2.3 basis points to 4.402%, the 10-year declined 3.7 basis points to 4.698% and the 30-year dropped 4.5 basis points to 5.227%. The 10-year real yield accounted for almost the entire nominal move, falling 3.4 basis points, while the breakeven eased only 0.3 basis point, indicating lower required real yields rather than a material improvement in the medium-term inflation outlook.

Oil provided immediate relief as WTI fell 2.16% and Brent lost 2.39% despite Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s threat of penalties against countries continuing to trade with Iran. The announcement lacked operational details and did not establish an additional loss of physical supply. Treasuries gained further after a report that officials were considering using part of Treasury’s $935 billion cash balance to buy older, higher-coupon securities, which could postpone the bill issuance otherwise needed to finance the repurchases.

Bessent said no bonds had yet been bought under the expanded program, regular auctions would continue and changes would not come before the quarterly refunding at the start of November. The close therefore reflected a more favorable possible funding method, not a commitment to use cash or a permanent reduction in federal borrowing. Gold rose 2.47%, while the Dollar Index gained 0.18% on the day but remained 0.66% lower over the week. Credit funds edged higher, but the S&P 500 fell 0.28%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.97% and semiconductors dropped 2.70% as investors reassessed the financing burden surrounding the AI investment boom.
overall_summary.summary: Falling crude and a report that Treasury might finance long-bond repurchases from its cash balance pulled intermediate and long yields lower, but near-unchanged breakevens and no policy commitment left the rally’s durability unresolved.
